item.title: ai: Content Understanding adds GPT-5.6, GPT-6, and GPT-6.1: Choose the right model for your workload
item.description:
Azure Content Understanding now supports the GPT-5.6, GPT-6, and GPT-6.1 model families for document, text, speech, and video workflows. Microsoft also updated its model recommendations to help users choose among the expanded set of supported models.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: ai: When one pass isn’t enough: agentic mode in Azure Content Understanding
item.description:
The post introduces agentic mode in Azure Content Understanding for harder document-analysis tasks that need more than a single pass. It also explains when to use agentic mode instead of standard mode.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: ai: From extraction to action: Using grounding and confidence to build reliable document workflows
item.description:
The post explains how Azure Content Understanding uses grounding, field-level confidence, and calibration to support reliable document workflows. It focuses on using these signals to prioritize human review and improve extraction quality.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: ai: Azure Content Understanding Prebuilt Analyzers: packaging domain knowledge for document AI
item.description:
Azure Content Understanding prebuilt analyzers package domain-specific document AI logic with grounding and confidence signals. The post also shares preview benchmark results for Advanced Contextualization, including quality, modeled cost, and latency.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: ai: Azure Document Intelligence and Azure Content Understanding: a practical guide
item.description:
The post compares Azure Document Intelligence and Azure Content Understanding, focusing on extraction architecture, workload fit, layout capabilities, deployment options, and how to evaluate which service to use. It is a practical guidance piece rather than a feature announcement.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: ai: Why content extraction still matters in the GenAI era
item.description:
The post argues that as AI models improve, reliable content extraction becomes more important for trustworthy downstream use. It also contrasts Azure Content Understanding and Azure Document Intelligence, and previews what is next.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog
